title.en: glTF material extension matrix: Principled BSDF to MeshPhysicalMaterial

en: which glTF material extensions survive export
clearcoat sheen specular anisotropy iridescence handoff

summary: Map each Principled BSDF surface feature to its KHR_materials_* extension and the three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial property that receives it, and check each row against what the exporter and the loader actually list as supported.
objective: Every advanced material feature in a scene names its glTF extension and its receiving renderer property, and any row without an exporter or loader path is declared before authoring rather than discovered after export.
intent_signals: my sheen material lost its look after export
map Principled BSDF inputs to glTF
iridescence does not export from Blender
example_prompts: Plan a car-paint material that survives Blender to glTF to three.js with clearcoat intact.
Tell me which advanced material features I can rely on end to end for this product viewer.
not_for: Claiming appearance equivalence between two renderers implementing the same extension.
Extensions no source in this record documents.

principles: A material feature only exists end to end when three separate lists agree: the exporter can write the extension, the extension defines the property, and the loader can read it. A row where any of the three is missing is an authoring decision, not a bug to debug later.

Extension factors and renderer properties are not always spelled the same. The glTF factor names carry the defaults; the renderer property names carry the runtime API. Write both in the same row so neither is guessed.
Defaults matter as much as names: several extensions default to the disabled value, so a material that exports without an authored factor produces a file that is valid and visually inert.
Use MeshPhysicalMaterial for any row in this matrix; the metallic-roughness baseline material has no properties to receive them and fails silently rather than loudly.
implementation: Clearcoat: Blender's `Clearcoat` and `Clearcoat Roughness` inputs on the Principled BSDF trigger `KHR_materials_clearcoat` (`clearcoatFactor` default `0.0`, `clearcoatRoughnessFactor` default `0.0`, plus `clearcoatNormalTexture`; textures pack clearcoat in `R` and clearcoat roughness in `G`) and arrive as `material.clearcoat`, `material.clearcoatRoughness`, `material.clearcoatNormalMap` and `material.clearcoatNormalScale`.

Sheen: the Blender sheen inputs export as `KHR_materials_sheen` (`sheenColorFactor` default `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]` in linear space, `sheenRoughnessFactor` default `0.0`, roughness carried in the texture's alpha channel) and arrive as `material.sheen`, `material.sheenColor`, `material.sheenRoughness`, `material.sheenColorMap` and `material.sheenRoughnessMap`. The loader page's supported-extension list does not name `KHR_materials_sheen`, so verify sheen import against the installed release before designing around it.

Specular: `Specular IOR Level` or `Specular Tint` triggers `KHR_materials_specular` (`specularFactor` default `1.0` with strength in the texture alpha, `specularColorFactor` default `[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]` as an F0 colour in linear RGB with the texture encoded in sRGB) and arrives as `material.specularIntensity`, `material.specularColor`, `material.specularIntensityMap` and `material.specularColorMap`.

Anisotropy: the `Anisotropic` and `Anisotropic Rotation` sockets, with the tangent socket linked to a tangent node using the normal map's UVMap, export as `KHR_materials_anisotropy` (`anisotropyStrength` default `0.0` multiplied by the texture's blue channel, `anisotropyRotation` default `0.0` radians counter-clockwise from the tangent, direction in the red and green channels) and arrive as `material.anisotropy` in 0.0-1.0, `material.anisotropyRotation` in radians and `material.anisotropyMap`.

Emissive strength: Blender writes `KHR_materials_emissive_strength` when any component of `emissiveFactor` exceeds 1.0; the extension's `emissiveStrength` defaults to `1.0` and multiplies the material's emissive value so emission can exceed [0, 1] for HDR rendering. On the renderer side the pair is `material.emissive` and `material.emissiveIntensity` (documented default `1`).

Iridescence: `KHR_materials_iridescence` defines `iridescenceFactor` default `0.0`, `iridescenceIor` default `1.3`, `iridescenceThicknessMinimum` default `100.0` nm and `iridescenceThicknessMaximum` default `400.0` nm, received as `material.iridescence`, `material.iridescenceIOR` and the two-element `material.iridescenceThicknessRange`. The exporter manual's supported-extension lists name no iridescence extension in either direction, so this row has no documented Blender export path: author it on the renderer side or add it with a post-export tool.

Transmission, volume and IOR: the `Transmission` input triggers `KHR_materials_transmission` (texture value in the `R` channel, Non-Color), volume requires transmission to be set first and rides `KHR_materials_volume`, and `KHR_materials_ior` carries the Principled IOR - the manual notes the importer sets the Principled BSDF IOR to 1.5 when the extension is absent. These arrive as `material.transmission`, `material.thickness`, `material.attenuationColor`, `material.attenuationDistance` and `material.ior`; see `knowledge.blender-three-thick-volume-handoff` and `knowledge.blender-three-transparency-boundaries` for the thickness and sorting contracts they depend on.

Variants: `KHR_materials_variants` declares a root-level `variants` array of named objects plus per-primitive `mappings` entries that pair a `material` index with an array of `variants` indices, each variant index used no more than once across the whole mappings array. The exporter manual lists it under both import and export, but the loader page places it under `The following glTF 2.0 extension is supported by an external user plugin` alongside `MSFT_texture_dds`, `KHR_animation_pointer` and `NEEDLE_progressive`, so a viewer must supply a plugin through `loader.register(callback)` rather than expect native switching.

Before authoring any row, check it against the loader's own native list: `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `KHR_lights_punctual`, `KHR_materials_anisotropy`, `KHR_materials_clearcoat`, `KHR_materials_dispersion`, `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`, `KHR_materials_ior`, `KHR_materials_specular`, `KHR_materials_transmission`, `KHR_materials_iridescence`, `KHR_materials_unlit`, `KHR_materials_volume`, `KHR_mesh_quantization`, `KHR_meshopt_compression`, `KHR_texture_basisu`, `KHR_texture_transform`, `EXT_materials_bump`, `EXT_meshopt_compression`, `EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing`, `EXT_texture_avif`, `EXT_texture_webp`.

Instantiate the receiving material as `new THREE.MeshPhysicalMaterial( { ... } )`. `MeshStandardMaterial` exposes only the metallic-roughness baseline (`map`, `roughness`, `metalness`, `roughnessMap`, `normalMap`, `normalScale`) and has no property to receive any factor in this matrix.
observable_checks: For every row used, the exported glTF names the extension in `extensionsUsed` and the loaded material reports a non-default value on the paired property; a property still sitting at its documented default means the extension did not survive the handoff.

A material authored only as `MeshStandardMaterial` shows no clearcoat, sheen or transmission response even when the glTF declares those extensions, which separates a loader problem from a material-class problem.
Changing `material.iridescenceThicknessRange` away from the extension's [100, 400] nm defaults changes the observed hue shift, confirming the two-element array is being read.

Without a registered plugin, switching a material variant leaves the primitive on its default `material` index and reports no error; the same asset with a plugin registered through `loader.register(callback)` switches.
An asset whose only sheen evidence is `sheenColorFactor` at its default `[0, 0, 0]` renders identically with and without the extension, which is the expected result rather than a failure.

known_limits: Every list quoted here is a documentation list as accessed: the exporter's supported extensions, the loader's native and plugin lists and the renderer's property set all change between releases and must be re-checked against installed versions.

The loader page's supported-extension list does not name KHR_materials_sheen and the exporter manual lists no iridescence extension; both are observations about those pages on the access date, not statements about any release's source code.
Extension conformance does not imply appearance agreement: two renderers implementing the same extension may still differ, and no comparison was rendered for this record.
The variants extension document says nothing about which engines import variants, so the plugin requirement here is taken from the loader page alone.
Authored reusable guidance: no export, load or render was performed for this record.
creative_affordances: Rows may be deliberately dropped for delivery weight; record the drop rather than leaving an inert factor in the file.
A row with no export path may be re-authored on the renderer side as a declared departure from the source asset.

claims.statement: The ratified Khronos material extensions define their factors and defaults as follows: clearcoatFactor 0.0 and clearcoatRoughnessFactor 0.0 with a clearcoatNormalTexture; sheenColorFactor [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] in linear space and sheenRoughnessFactor 0.0 with roughness carried in a texture alpha channel; specularFactor 1.0 with strength in a texture alpha channel and specularColorFactor [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] as an F0 colour in linear RGB whose texture is encoded in sRGB; anisotropyStrength 0.0 multiplied by a texture blue channel and anisotropyRotation 0.0 radians counter-clockwise from the tangent; emissiveStrength 1.0 multiplying the material's emissive value; and iridescenceFactor 0.0, iridescenceIor 1.3, iridescenceThicknessMinimum 100.0 nanometres and iridescenceThicknessMaximum 400.0 nanometres.
claims.scope: Property names, units and defaults declared by the accessed ratified extension documents. They define file-format semantics, not any renderer's shading result.

claims.statement: The MeshPhysicalMaterial documentation lists the receiving properties clearcoat, clearcoatRoughness, clearcoatNormalMap and clearcoatNormalScale; sheen, sheenColor, sheenRoughness, sheenColorMap and sheenRoughnessMap; specularIntensity, specularColor, specularIntensityMap and specularColorMap; anisotropy from 0.0 to 1.0, anisotropyRotation measured in radians counter-clockwise from the tangent, and anisotropyMap; iridescence, iridescenceIOR and iridescenceThicknessRange as an array of exactly two elements giving minimum and maximum thickness; and transmission, thickness, attenuationColor, attenuationDistance, ior and dispersion.
claims.scope: Documented property names and stated ranges of one unversioned library page as accessed. It does not state how those properties are shaded or that they match another renderer.

claims.statement: The loader page publishes two separate lists: a set of glTF 2.0 extensions the loader supports directly, which includes KHR_materials_anisotropy, KHR_materials_clearcoat, KHR_materials_emissive_strength, KHR_materials_ior, KHR_materials_specular, KHR_materials_transmission, KHR_materials_iridescence and KHR_materials_volume but does not name KHR_materials_sheen, and a set supported by an external user plugin, which contains KHR_materials_variants, MSFT_texture_dds, KHR_animation_pointer and NEEDLE_progressive; plugins are attached through the loader's register(callback) method.
claims.scope: The two documented extension lists on the accessed unversioned loader page. The absence of an entry is an observation about the list, not about a release's source code.

source_refs.locator: "GLTFLoader supports the following glTF 2.0 extensions:" list including KHR_lights_punctual, KHR_materials_anisotropy, KHR_materials_clearcoat, KHR_materials_emissive_strength, KHR_materials_ior, KHR_materials_specular, KHR_materials_transmission, KHR_materials_iridescence, KHR_materials_volume, KHR_meshopt_compression, EXT_meshopt_compression

"The following glTF 2.0 extension is supported by an external user plugin:" KHR_materials_variants, MSFT_texture_dds, KHR_animation_pointer, NEEDLE_progressive; .register(callback) "Registers a plugin callback"; the supported-extension list above it does not name KHR_materials_sheen

claims.statement: The Blender glTF exporter manual documents which Principled BSDF inputs trigger which extensions - Clearcoat and Clearcoat Roughness for KHR_materials_clearcoat with clearcoat in the red and clearcoat roughness in the green channel, a sheen roughness texture written to the alpha channel for KHR_materials_sheen, Specular IOR Level or Specular Tint for KHR_materials_specular, the Anisotropic and Anisotropic Rotation sockets for KHR_materials_anisotropy, an emissiveFactor component greater than 1.0 for KHR_materials_emissive_strength, the Transmission input for KHR_materials_transmission with volume requiring transmission, and KHR_materials_ior with an implied Principled IOR of 1.5 when the extension is absent - and its list of directly supported extensions names no iridescence extension in either the import or the export direction.
claims.scope: Documented exporter behaviour and supported-extension lists on the accessed 4.5 LTS add-on manual page. Support lists change between Blender versions.

source_refs.locator: Materials sections: Clearcoat ("When the Clearcoat input on the Principled BSDF node has a nonzero default value or Image Texture node connected, the KHR_materials_clearcoat glTF extension will be included in the export", clearcoat in R and Clearcoat Roughness in G); Sheen ("If a Sheen Roughness Texture is used, glTF requires the values be written to the alpha (A) channel"); Specular ("When the Specular IOR Level or Specular Tint input of Principled BSDF node have a non default value ... KHR_materials_specular"); Anisotropy (Anisotropic and Anisotropic Rotation sockets, tangent socket linked to a tangent node with the normal map's UVMap); Emission ("If any component of emissiveFactor is > 1.0, KHR_materials_emissive_strength extension will be used"); Transmission and Volume; IOR ("if KHR_materials_ior is not set, IOR value of Principled BSDF node is set to 1.5"); Extensions > Export list: KHR_draco_mesh_compression, KHR_lights_punctual, KHR_materials_clearcoat, KHR_materials_transmission, KHR_materials_unlit, KHR_materials_emissive_strength, KHR_materials_volume, KHR_materials_sheen, KHR_materials_specular, KHR_materials_anisotropy, KHR_materials_ior, KHR_materials_variants, KHR_texture_transform, EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing (no iridescence entry in either the Import or the Export list)

claims.statement: KHR_materials_variants defines two properties, a variants array on the glTF root holding objects each with a name, and mappings on any number of mesh primitives whose entries each specify a material by its index and an array of variant indices, with the constraint that across the entire mappings array each variant index must be used no more than one time.
claims.scope: The ratified extension's declared structure and constraint. The document states nothing about which engines or loaders import variants.

source_refs.locator: Properties > Variants and Mappings: "defines two properties - variants on the root node and mappings on any number of primitive nodes"; variants defined at the glTF root as an array of objects each with a name property; each mapping item specifies a material by index and an array of variants indices; "Across the entire mappings array, each variant index must be used no more than one time"
